title: A recommender that records why it recommended, and is judged on it
status: Design complete and reviewed; Milestone 2 data work is under way.

overview.question: Can a carefully tuned, leakage-safe pipeline predict the next rating a user submits on MovieLens 1M better than a well-tuned simple baseline, and can it show that with honest intervals?
overview.summary: Every phase is fixed before any result is seen: the split, the baselines, the tuning budget and the conclusion's possible verdicts. {models} predictive models climb from simple linear regression to stacking, each judged against a regularised bias model under the same budget, with uncertainty clustered by user.

milestones.focus: Form a group of three to five and submit project preferences.

milestones.name: Data wrangling and project redefinition
milestones.focus: Get, load and clean the data, then restate the project question it can answer. milestones.name: Final modeling and deliverables
milestones.focus: Final models, findings and limitations; a 2,000 to 2,500 word report, a 6-minute video and the commented notebook.

scope.principle: The timestamps record when a rating was submitted, not when a movie was watched. Every question, feature and metric concerns rating submissions.

phases.title: Scope, fixed before anything runs
points: Question, unit and target declared in writing before any code.
Target: rating in {1..5}, ordinal, modelled as continuous — a limitation tested by {model:14}, not only recorded.
Metrics: RMSE, MAE, and the macro-averaged MAEᴹ and RMSEᴹ, which an imbalanced ordinal target requires, as {technique:3} shows.
Predictions left unrounded, so figures stay comparable with published work.

phases.title: Structural audit (all rows)
points: {technique:1}, first half: the structure of every row, never a rating value.
Load with latin-1; movies.dat is not UTF-8.
Shape, types, duplicates, target sanity, referential integrity.
The README's own claims checked, not assumed: whole-star ratings, at least 20 ratings per user, IDs within their stated ranges, and duplicate or test movie entries.
Distinguish {moviesRated} movies that were rated from {moviesListed} rows in movies.dat.
Timestamp to datetime; confirm the {firstMonth} – {lastMonth} span.
Leakage scan: per-user first and last rating; cumulative ratings over time.

phases.title: Split design — before any feature is computed
points: Tₜₑₛₜ at the 0.9 quantile of rating timestamps; Tᵥₐₗ at the 0.8 quantile. A quantile, never a calendar date.
Protocol A — global temporal split. The real protocol.
Protocol B — per-user last-k. Leaks across users; what most published work does.
Protocol C — random k-fold. The ceiling of optimism.
{technique:5}: folds subdivide the training window only, in time order, compared against random k-fold.
Sensitivity across quantiles 0.8 / 0.85 / 0.9 / 0.95.
Cost accounting: users and movies that survive A but not B.
Leakage assertions, including the count of training ratings that postdate a test rating under B — the leak, quantified.

Two times per rating: event time, when the user rated the movie, and observation time, when the system learned of it. MovieLens 1M records only event time, so the replay's observation-time assumption is declared, not measured (A.300).

phases.title: Distributional EDA (training window only)
points: {technique:1}, second half: rating values, inside the training window only.
Ratings per month; per-user active-span histogram; rating distribution and skew.
Long tails by movie and by user; demographics coverage, zip in aggregate only.
Genre matrix, 18 binary columns.
Post-split health checks on each subset: timestamp collisions, user lifetimes, and the cold users and movies the split creates.
Deliverable: a risk register and a preprocessing plan — not a folder of plots.

phases.title: Leakage-safe feature engineering
points: One control, applied uniformly: rolling, time-ordered cross-fitting. Random out-of-fold folds would reintroduce exactly what Phase 2 removed.
User and movie history: count, mean, std, median, Q20, Q80 of prior ratings; recency.
{technique:2}: target-encoded means with smoothing toward the global mean, fitted inside the fold, which handles cold users and movies without a special case.
Content, static and context features carry no target and need no control.
{technique:4} on the 18-column genre block, fitted inside the fold.
Each feature's provenance recorded: when it becomes known relative to the rating it predicts.
Two feature views of the same statistics: one-hot for the linear rungs, target-encoded for the tree rungs.
Diagnostics with pass thresholds: permuted target (< 1% advantage), shuffled groups (no advantage), temporal boundary assertion.

Point-in-time correctness, stricter than a feature store's inclusive bound: every feature for a rating is built only from ratings dated strictly before it, since MovieLens timestamps collide at one-second resolution (A.292).

phases.title: Baselines — the real opponent
points: Global mean, user mean, movie mean.
Regularised bias model with its own tuned penalties — the opponent.
The bias is the user and movie offsets fitted on the training window only; {model:13} estimates their shrinkage from the data instead of tuning it.
Computed under all three protocols; a baseline's value is protocol-specific.
Tuning budget declared before fitting, identical for the baseline and for the last model.
The primary comparison and its three possible verdicts are written here, before any result is seen.

phases.title: The linear family
points: {model:1}, then {model:2}, then {model:3}: interactions and polynomial count terms.
Centre continuous predictors; measure VIF before and after interacting, threshold 5.
For the genre block and other factor terms, the adjusted GVIF is read against the threshold, not the raw VIF.
Residuals vs fitted will show five diagonal bands — an artefact of a five-level target, not non-linearity.
{technique:6}: the real diagnostic is shrinkage in predicted-vs-observed, and accepting it is a bias–variance decision.
A bounded ordinal cannot be log-transformed, so the usual heteroscedasticity remedy does not apply.
Count predictions outside [1,5]; report clipped and unclipped.

phases.title: Regularisation
points: Standardisation inside the fold — mandatory, since the penalty treats all coefficients alike.
{model:4}, {model:5} and the elastic net between them over ~100 penalties, the mixing weight tuned with the penalty on the same time-ordered folds, selected by the one-standard-error rule.
Stability selection over half-sample bootstraps, {technique:9}: a selection frequency per feature.
Correlated groups flagged, with the member lasso happened to pick.
{model:13} estimates the user and movie shrinkage from their variance components instead of a tuned penalty.
{technique:6}: train and validation error against complexity — the bias–variance figure as computable evidence.

phases.title: kNN regression
points: {model:6}: the prediction is stated first, at ~900k rows and 50+ features, kNN is outside its documented range on both axes. The phase tests that claim.
Distance treated as a tuned choice: Euclidean, Manhattan, Gower.
Features standardised inside the fold before any distance is taken; distance weighting as a tuned option; query cost reported, since tree indexes degrade beyond about 10 dimensions.
{technique:4} first, then kNN — the documented remedy; accuracy and time reported.
Error against retained components, crossing the ~30–40 feature mark: the curse of dimensionality drawn from this project's own data.

phases.title: Trees
points: Continuous features win splits over binary ones by construction, so genre dummies will rarely be chosen.
{model:7}: stopping conditions and cost-complexity pruning, alpha by time-aware CV; under 100 leaves for the readable version.
{technique:8}: permutation importance on the temporal validation set, never the default impurity measure; correlated features permuted together, since they split the credit.
Refit without the target-encoded means: what does the tree use when it is not handed the answer?
A tree cannot predict outside its training range.

phases.title: Ensembles
points: {model:8}: variance reduction against the single tree, over repeated seeds.
{technique:7}: OOB compared against the temporal validation, not against random CV; the gap is the finding.
{model:9} with subsample size and feature count declared, not defaulted.
{model:10}: each round reweights the rows toward the largest errors, and its trees are combined by a weighted median, judged on the same temporal validation.
{technique:8}: permutation importance tests the published 35% / 30% user-versus-movie split rather than assuming it.
{model:11} with early stopping on the temporal validation set, never the library's built-in random validation fraction; staged error curve; residual fitting shown on one worked example.

phases.title: Stacking
points: {model:12}: diversity measured first, the correlation matrix of out-of-fold predictions.
Out-of-fold predictions by time-ordered folds.
Non-negative ridge meta-learner, not ordinary least squares.
The weights are reported as a model-selection verdict: which rungs survived, which were zeroed.
Does the ensemble beat its best member and a simple average of the rungs, with intervals?

phases.title: Uncertainty and significance
points: {technique:9}: bootstrap clustered by user, not by row: ~100k test ratings come from at most {users} users.
The naive row-level interval reported beside the clustered one, so the cost of clustering is visible.
Per-model intervals are descriptive and labelled “not a test”.
The primary comparison — best model against the regularised bias baseline — is paired, user-clustered, and pre-specified in Phase 4: {technique:10}.
All other pairs form an exploratory family under Holm correction.
{technique:12}: the primary comparison also tested by flipping the signs of the per-user differences, with the symmetry that test assumes checked rather than assumed.
Coefficient tests for the unregularised model only; the post-selection limitation stated.
Prediction intervals, and seed spread kept separate from sampling uncertainty.
{technique:11}: the prediction intervals audited for empirical against nominal coverage, overall and by user activity group, with their width and interval score.

phases.title: Diagnostics
points: Every check here is exploratory and descriptive, declared in advance.
Leakage audit; calibration reliability diagram — predicted vs observed by decile, with the calibration slope and intercept and calibration-in-the-large.
Cold user and cold movie, threshold declared with its reason plus sensitivity.
{technique:3}: error by rating value, read beside MAEᴹ.
Error by activity decile tested for a monotone trend.
{model:14} refits the target as ordered categories, its proportional-odds assumption checked by the Brant test; if the conclusion changes, the continuous treatment mattered.
Failure taxonomy: which kinds of rating are missed.
The optimism gap from four mechanisms: Protocol C, Protocol B, OOB, random k-fold.

phases.title: Report
points: Structured on the REFORMS checklist: leakage, evaluation design and uncertainty.
Each statistical test's assumptions checked and reported, and the contexts where the findings are not expected to hold named, as the checklist asks.
Reproducibility record: every seed, grid and budget, the data version, the environment, the wall-clock cost.
The pre-specified conclusion resolved, including the row that says the baseline was not beaten.
Model card; limitations stated plainly, including that these conclusions concern {users} users between {firstYear} and {lastYear}.
Lineage recorded as OpenLineage run events, so every reported number traces back to the three MovieLens files (A.293).

models.name: Ordinal regression, a cumulative link model

baseline_note: A well-tuned simple baseline is hard to beat on dense rating data, and an under-tuned one makes the whole comparison an artefact of how the tuning budget was spent. So the bias model gets its own tuned penalties and the same budget as {model:12}.

evidence.principle: A recommendation is a traceable decision with supporting evidence, not merely a number a model returns.

disciplines.name: Reproducible machine learning
disciplines.question: Can the experiment and its results be reconstructed?
disciplines.now: Every seed, grid and tuning budget is declared before fitting, and every lab runs on seeded data.

disciplines.name: Decision provenance
disciplines.question: Which data, features, model and rules produced a result?
disciplines.now: Each milestone result already names its evidence contract and digest, and every repository task run is recorded in a signed, hash-chained ledger.

disciplines.name: Explainability
disciplines.question: Which factors influenced a prediction?
disciplines.now: Coefficients for the linear rungs and permutation importance on the temporal validation set are part of the design.

disciplines.name: Objective evaluation
disciplines.question: Does a model beat an appropriate baseline under a fair protocol?
disciplines.now: The temporal split, the tuned bias baseline, the shared tuning budget and the paired, user-clustered primary test are fixed before any result is seen.

disciplines.name: Causal evaluation
disciplines.question: Did showing a recommendation change what users did?
disciplines.now: MovieLens 1M records submitted ratings, not what users were shown, so there is no exposure to estimate an effect from.
disciplines.why: The reviewer removed real-user logging, off-policy evaluation and the Open Bandit Dataset, so the acceptance gate refuses any claim of changed user behaviour (A.285).

disciplines.name: Continuous evaluation
disciplines.question: Does a conclusion still hold on later data?
disciplines.now: Phase 2 already tests the split at four quantiles. No system is deployed, so post-deployment monitoring is outside the TF's scope; later time windows are re-judged offline instead.

disciplines.name: Policy-based governance
disciplines.question: Does an explicit, auditable rule decide whether the evidence is sufficient?
disciplines.now: The primary comparison and its three possible verdicts are written in Phase 4, before any result is seen.

overview.note: A recommendation is a traceable decision with supporting evidence, not merely a number a model returns. Every conclusion this project reports passes through one chain, offline and within the TF's scope: a policy written as code judges evidence recorded as data, and only its verdict becomes a reported decision.

evidence.prediction_note: Every number on this page measures how well a model predicts the next rating a user submits. A well-predicted rating is not evidence that recommending a movie adds value: that is a causal question, and it needs exposure to recommendations, which MovieLens 1M does not record.

practices.practice: A recommender is itself evaluated as a treatment, by an experimentation stack separate from the one that builds it
practices.here: Offline, the evaluator alone holds the split, the held-out ratings and the metric code, and each model only returns predictions.

practices.practice: A/B tests across several objectives, including long-term satisfaction
practices.here: No live users exist here to experiment on.
practices.why: Online experimentation needs real users, which the TF's offline scope excludes.

practices.practice: Predicting what someone likes is not proof that recommending it adds value
practices.here: Results says so beside its numbers, and the gate refuses any claim of changed behaviour; Netflix's popularity benchmark mirrors this project's movie-mean baseline.

practices.practice: Metrics linked to the model and the dataset they were measured on
practices.here: Each evidence record links every metric to the fitted model's identity and the dataset's digest, offline, without an MLflow server.
Stricter than Feast's inclusive bound: each feature comes only from ratings dated strictly before its target, since MovieLens timestamps collide.

practices.practice: Lineage as structured run events with dataset facets
practices.here: Each offline stage writes START and COMPLETE events as files, so every result traces back to the three MovieLens files.

practices.practice: Conversational recommendation agents, tested on live listeners
practices.here: No application or agent is built here.
practices.why: An application and an online recommender are outside the TF's scope.
